front: What do the two vertical rails of a ladder diagram represent?
back: The two opposite poles of the power supply; every rung is connected between them.
excerpt: and attach to opposite poles of a power supply, usually 120 volts AC
mnemonic: A ladder's two side rails hold up every rung; the two supply poles feed every rung.

front: What does each horizontal rung of a ladder diagram represent?
back: One control circuit: a separate parallel branch connected between the two poles of the power supply.
excerpt: each one representing a unique parallel circuit branch between the poles of the power supply

front: Why was PLC control logic drawn as ladder diagrams rather than written in a general-purpose computer language?
back: So factory engineers and technicians, already familiar with relay diagrams, could write the software without extra training in a language such as FORTRAN.
excerpt: to allow factory engineers and technicians to develop software without additional training to learn a language such as FORTRAN or other general-purpose computer language

front: When does a normally open contact --[ ]-- in a ladder program pass power?
back: When the Boolean variable it reads is TRUE; while the variable is FALSE it blocks power.
excerpt: When start_button is TRUE, power flows through and motor_run becomes TRUE.

front: When does a normally closed contact --[/]-- in a ladder program pass power?
back: When its variable is FALSE; it blocks power when the variable is TRUE, acting as a logical NOT.
excerpt: It passes power when its variable is FALSE and blocks power when TRUE.
mnemonic: The slash in --[/]-- crosses the signal out: it conducts when the bit is NOT true.

front: A ladder diagram draws every contact in its 'normal' condition. Which state is that?
back: The state it has while its device is not energized (at rest); the contact changes state when the device is energized.
excerpt: An NC contact would be shown as normally closed, and an NO contact would appear as a normally open device. All contacts associated with a device will change state when the device is energized.
mnemonic: Normal = nobody touching it, no power on it: the device asleep on the shelf.

front: Which logic function do two contacts wired in series on a rung perform?
back: AND: power gets through only if both contacts are closed at the same time.
excerpt: We can mimic the AND logic function by wiring the two contacts in series instead of parallel
mnemonic: Series = one gate after another: this AND that must both be open to walk through.

front: Which logic function do two contacts wired in parallel on a rung perform?
back: OR: the output energizes if at least one of the contacts is closed, since either one gives a path for current.
excerpt: Parallel contacts are logically equivalent to an OR gate.
mnemonic: Parallel = two doors side by side: this OR that one lets you through.

front: How many contacts in a ladder program may refer to the same bit?
back: Any number: a ladder program can refer to a single bit's status any number of times, like a relay with an indefinitely large number of contacts.
excerpt: a ladder program can refer any number of times to the status of a single bit, equivalent to a relay with an indefinitely large number of contacts

front: What does a regular coil --( )-- write to its variable on every scan?
back: The rung's power state: TRUE if power reaches the coil, FALSE if it does not.
excerpt: Key characteristic: The variable is updated every scan cycle. It follows the rung state in real time.

front: In what order does a PLC execute the rungs of a ladder program?
back: From top to bottom, one rung after another.
excerpt: the last one evaluated wins (since rungs execute top to bottom)

front: How can the result of one rung be used by the rungs evaluated after it?
back: Its output coil's bit can be read as an input by contacts in the rungs that follow.
excerpt: the output coil of a rung may feed into the next stage of the ladder as an input
